subject: A heart sent from the 'Belonging' stage - and a politics that calls it a 'strange thing'
alt: Satish Acharya's cartoon: a television screen, its black frame and the wire from a wall socket making the set clear, shows the launch of Sonia Gandhi's book 'Belonging'. On the left, Rahul Gandhi, bearded and in a white kurta, stands at a lectern with a microphone; his eyes are closed and he purses his lips as he sends a small red heart flying from his open palm, with little white clouds drifting ahead of it. On the right, Sonia Gandhi, grey-haired in a purple sari with gold dots, sits smiling; a book marked 'BELONGING' lies on the desk before her. Outside the screen, below, are two men seen from behind and in profile: at the left a man with a tricolour shawl over his head, and at the right a man in glasses and a saffron shawl, his mouth open. Their speech bubbles read 'WHAT'S THAT STRANGE THING?' and 'DISGUSTING!'. Satish Acharya's signature is at the lower right.
chutki: On television is the launch of Sonia Gandhi's book 'Belonging: A Journey of Love'. Rahul Gandhi sends a red heart from his hand and Sonia, seated before him, smiles. The two men watching cannot place it: one asks, 'What's that strange thing?' and the other says, 'Disgusting!'

The needle is that a stage built around a book of love leaves the people watching it with only two words for love - strange and disgusting. Politics has turned every feeling into a slogan, so a plain heart now looks like an exotic object; and those who call it disgusting are perhaps afraid that the language of the heart will be understood better than their slogans.
